native_findings.finding: cmdCaptions/runCaptions do not acquire their own project lease or check STOP; the reviewed external one-use wrapper must do both before calling normal native main once.

Native runCaptions may write nine SRT/VTT pairs, captions/manifest.json, and append one state.json caption run. It may remove not-written target files; the wrapper must reject any deletion outside its exact allowlist and any incomplete locale set.

currentDub checks script/translation/voice/raw/branding currency but does not approve failed ASR. Native current EN/JA physical timelines therefore remain valid timing inputs while their voices stay failed/stopped. Missing PT/ID/VI/TH dub timelines fall back to the presented primary narration.

Native caption CLI exit0 is based on chapter problems only. A true caption result also requires actual manifest skipped/missing state, parsed-file diagnostics, deterministic native expected-byte comparison, current source line coverage and the existing captionsItem component.
Native captionsItem treats reading-speed warnings as warnings; every other cue issue is a failure. Preserve all returned diagnostics and do not label a result with warnings as zero problems.

state.json is reserialized after one appended run. Compare all non-runs properties, the exact original run prefix, exactly one added run with only stage/at/locales and the actual native timestamp/manifest locale order. A raw-byte prefix check would be wrong.

parseSrt does not retain cue.line IDs, so its diagnostic labels contain (?) while native manifest problems retain source IDs. Preserve the two diagnostics independently; compare manifest problems to native expected cues, not literal parsed-SRT labels.

Caption-current context includes brandingCurrent, actual body frame count and speech bindings. A complete caption-only component check can reuse this predicate without running full qa, replacing review/qa.json or contacting models.
